note: A document and three attachments through the WRITE path. It is the only case in the corpus that proves attachments round-trip through a container. What a runner compares is the root document's tree, the entry names, the attachment bodies, and that the document is the first entry: section 7.1 constrains those and leaves every other field of the archive to the writer, so the bytes are not compared and two conforming writers are not expected to agree on them. The entry list is chosen and not tidy, and it is the load-bearing part of the case. `Ｚ.txt` begins U+FF3A and `😀.txt` begins U+1F600, one below U+FFFF and one above it, so the entry names reach what an ASCII-only set never does: the UTF-8 filename flag, a surrogate pair in a name, and whatever a language's own string handling makes of both. If the attachment set is ever reduced, keep one name above U+FFFF beside one in U+E000 to U+FFFF. The archive must be produced through the write path, never by repackaging a decoded container, which reproduces what the input carried instead of applying the emit-boundary rules. A runner may feed these three attachments in any order and the case must pass whichever it was, so it is fed them reversed: where the attachments fall among themselves is not a rule, and the root document's position is. The attachments are carried in a JSON manifest rather than as real files beside this sidecar, deliberately: a name holding U+1F600 is subject to filesystem Unicode normalisation and case folding, so a checked-out file could differ from the name the case means. Inside JSON the name is escaped text and no filesystem can alter it.
